facts.claim: A no-confidence motion is the direct and decisive parliamentary device for testing collective responsibility of the Union Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha.
facts.laxmikanth: Ch13 collective responsibility; Ch23 executive control

facts.claim: Parliamentary government links political executive accountability to the popular House; it does not create watertight legislative-executive separation.
President is the de jure or nominal executive; the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister is the real political executive.
The Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
British parliamentary sovereignty differs from Indian constitutional supremacy and judicial review.
A minister who is not a member of either House for six consecutive months ceases to be a minister.
facts.laxmikanth: Ch13 membership distinction; validate with Article 75(5)

facts.claim: Checks and balances combine separated institutional roles with reciprocal controls such as veto, legislative participation in specified acts and judicial review.
facts.laxmikanth: Ch13 presidential comparison; Ch26 judicial review structure

facts.claim: Legislature primarily makes law, executive implements policy/law, judiciary adjudicates and interprets law; functions are not absolutely sealed.
Fusion of executive and legislature in parliamentary government accompanies political responsibility to the popular House.
Constitutional checks permit each organ to perform its core role while interacting within constitutional limits.
Parliamentary government operates at Union and State levels; Union Council is responsible to Lok Sabha and State Council to Legislative Assembly.
